entries.title: Novig operator Ludlow Exchange sues Ohio Attorney General and Casino Control Commission officials over sports event contracts
entries.facts: A complaint captioned LUDLOW EXCHANGE, LLC d/b/a NOVIG and titled COMPLAINT FOR DECLARATORY AND INJUNCTIVE RELIEF was filed in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Ohio, with page headers stamped Filed: 11/16/26 and an ECF header reading Case: 1:26-cv-03009. The named defendants, all sued in their official capacities, are Ohio Attorney General Andy Wilson, Ohio Casino Control Commission Interim Executive Director Andromeda Morrison, and commissioners Thomas J. Stickrath, Penelope Cunningham, Sheetal Bajoria, Scott Borgemenke, Triffon Callos, Keith Cheney and Christopher Smitherman. The complaint alleges that the Commodity Exchange Act impliedly preempts Ohio's gambling laws as applied to Novig, resting on the exclusive jurisdiction provision at 7 U.S.C. section 2(a)(1)(A), states that the federal question is whether the Commodity Exchange Act preempts Ohio's sports gaming and gambling laws, and alleges that Ohio's sports gaming regime discriminates against interstate commerce. It states that the Commission, through its Interim Executive Director, issued a cease-and-desist letter to Novig, and quotes that letter as stating that Novig is operating online sports gaming and is clearly engaged in bookmaking or facilitating bookmaking in violation of Ohio civil and criminal law. It cites KalshiEX LLC v. Schuler, 2026 WL 2884087 (6th Cir. Sept. 25, 2026) and states that Schuler is not final, that a petition for rehearing en banc is pending before the Sixth Circuit, and that three petitions for certiorari presenting the same preemption question are pending before the Supreme Court. It cites Further Definition of Swap to Exclude Casino-Style Gambling Products, 91 Fed. Reg. 65,969 (Oct. 19, 2026), and states that on June 16, 2026 the CFTC designated Novig as a designated contract market. The complaint was retrieved and read for pages 1 to 18 of 53; the counts and the prayer for relief are in the portion not read and are not described here.
entries.source_label: Complaint, Ludlow Exchange LLC v. Wilson, N.D. Ohio (court filing via CourtListener RECAP)

entries.title: CFTC Chairman reports approval of a designated contract market designation and derivatives clearing organization registration for a firm using blockchain-based architecture
entries.facts: In a statement titled Statement on American Innovation and the Future of Market Infrastructure, dated Washington, DC, November 16, 2026, CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig states that the CFTC approved the applications for designation as a designated contract market and registration as a derivatives clearing organization for a firm utilizing blockchain-based architecture for execution and settlement of derivatives contracts. The statement does not name the firm and does not reproduce the approval orders. It states that firms employing novel technologies must satisfy the same regulatory standards as traditional market infrastructure, listing anti-money-laundering programs, customer protection and segregation, market surveillance, financial resources, risk management and system safeguards, states that blockchain-native considerations may sometimes need to be addressed, and states that the Commodity Exchange Act's core principles apply without prescribing a particular technological architecture. The statement announces no rule, no comment period and no deadline.
entries.source_label: CFTC, Statement of Chairman Michael S. Selig, November 16, 2026
entries.relevant_to: derivatives exchanges, clearing organizations, tokenized market infrastructure providers, crypto trading platforms

entries.title: CFTC Announces Agenda for December Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
entries.facts: CFTC Release Number 9327-26, dated November 17, 2026, announces the agenda for a roundtable on 24/7 trading. The release states that the roundtable is taking place Dec. 15 from 1 to 4 p.m. EST at CFTC Headquarters, Three Lafayette Centre, 1155 21st St., NW, Washington, D.C., and that among other topics attendees will discuss issues related to the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight and weekend trading, tokenization and margin. The release states that the meeting is open to the public and will be livestreamed on CFTC.gov, and lists dial-in information and a webinar ID. It links an agenda document and cross-references Press Release Number 9318-26. No comment deadline and no registration deadline is stated.
entries.relevant_to: derivatives exchanges, clearing organizations, crypto trading platforms, tokenization providers
